cache_contract.description: MCP clients cache tools/list at session start; adding/renaming this tool requires a cache-refresh notice in status.md.
cache_contract._note: SEC-42 (OPS-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-LOW-W2): was a bare STRING. build-knowledge-json.mjs only projects cache_contract when it is an OBJECT, so the public bundle silently dropped it. Wrapped, preserving the original text verbatim under `description`.

drift_check_command: rm -rf dist && npm run build && grep -q "get_equity_regime" dist/index.js && ! grep -RnE '"(outcome_return_pct|outcome_price)"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*[-0-9.]' dist/lib/equities/equity-tool-formatters.js && echo SHAPE_OK
drift_check_note: SEC-42 (OPS-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-LOW-W1/W2): this check COULD NEVER PRINT SHAPE_OK. It grepped the BARE FIELD NAMES, and equity-tool-formatters.js line 12 carries a comment reading "outcome_return_pct / outcome_price can never appear because they are never ..." — so the grep matched the comment, `!` inverted it to false, and the && chain short-circuited. The file's own comment documenting that the fields never appear is what broke the check verifying they never appear. Now uses the value-binding regex CLAUDE.md prescribes, which matches a KEY:VALUE pair and is therefore blind to prose. Proven both directions by tests/unit/shape-snapshot-drift-checks.test.ts.
projection_note: SEC-42 (OPS-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-LOW-W2): scripts/build-knowledge-json.mjs projects this file into the PUBLIC knowledge bundle and reads the field name `snapshot_date`, with a TOTAL per-field fallback. This file carried its date under a different key, so the public bundle advertised snapshot_date:'unknown' (and, where allowed_keys/endpoint were absent, allowed_keys:[] and the filename as the endpoint) with a perfectly green build. Canonical keys added; the original keys are retained so no other reader breaks.
